do_more: Use direct, action-oriented quotes or provocative statements as title hooks (e.g., 'Know your enemy', 'You can turn over a new leaf every hour if you choose').
Focus topics heavily on conflict, strategy, personal control, and daily mental discipline (e.g., Sun Tzu, Stoicism, pessimism, shutting off mental steam).
Keep video length strictly around standard 40-42 second mark, as top performing videos yield high retention and re-watch loops (300%+ avgPercent) with structured quote analysis.
Target specific named authors or well-known classical texts in the first 3 seconds (e.g., Plato, Sun Tzu, Bacon).
avoid: Avoid generic or passive rhetorical questions as titles, such as 'Is faith rational?' or 'Can you be truly honest?'.
Stop using 'in 60 Seconds' formatting, book summary templates, or heavy emoji spam in titles which underperform across all metrics.
Avoid abstract, overly academic philosophical framing that lacks a direct personal application for the viewer.
short.title_style: Winning titles either state an intriguing, direct quote/instruction or name drop a famous historical figure with a clear warning/lesson.
next_tests: Test standard-length (~40s) shorts featuring high-aggression quotes from Marcus Aurelius using simple direct command titles vs. question titles.
Experiment with a 2-part format opening immediately with a shocking philosophical line from Nietzsche, skipping intro setup entirely.

full.title_style: Pose a concise, curiosity‑punch question that challenges a common belief and often cites a known book or concept
